column7: JSONLoader logs malformed rows to OSLog and skips them; a corrupt dataset shrinks and still reports a clean aggregate.
Session 335 presents Cohen's kappa as built-in; MetricsAggregator has no agreement statistic — Apple hand-writes 72 lines.
targetCount is a total: 13 seeds + 100 yields 87 new samples, and a target below your current count generates zero, silently.
TOC: the guide's collected silent failures — shrinking datasets, collapsed distributions, mismatched configs, orphan metrics.
Apple's snippet shadows Metric('Match') in the closure — same-name metrics merge or produce results aggregation never finds.
An eval whose model config differs from the app's (guardrails, options) scores a system you don't ship, and stays green.
(3...8).contains reads 100% for a constant 8 — @Guide(.count(3...8)) fixed the range and collapsed the distribution unseen.
The evaluates trait's second parameter is info: [String: String]; session 298 calls it 'notes' — trust the API spelling.
Reconstructions show func f(results:); the real shape is plain func f() reading EvaluationContext.current.result, singular.
ScoreDimension text differs between production and calibration on purpose — 'same evaluator' means same type, not same prompt.
Give the judge only a few alignment examples; a longer list overfits the alignment score and hides misalignment (335:210).
A broken evaluation still produces a number — the number you decided to trust; the catalogue below runs worst-first.
A 100-row file with 63 undecodable rows loads 37, runs cleanly and reports a green aggregate; only OSLog records the drops.
Overview: judge-alignment silent failures — unvalidated positional join, ?? 0 phantom ratings, undefined kappa read as zero.
TOC: silent failures in judge alignment (section 19).
numeric(_:) takes [Double: String]; Apple's sample writes integer literals that coerce — both work, dumps say Double.
reference returns [String: String] — each pair a labelled prompt section — not the String circulating material claims.
Omit ModelJudgePrompt and the judge falls back to defaultInstructions — stable, plausible scores with zero app context.
Judge drift never throws and grows with your dataset; the only detector is the kappa calibration you must build yourself.
Cohen's kappa is not in the framework despite session 335; Book Tracker hand-writes 72 lines in Statistics.swift.
Calibration contamination raises kappa — the judge looks better the more you break it, then ships behind a green test.
Section index: eight silent failures in judge alignment, from the positional join to inherited FM failure modes.
Expert and judge scores pair by index; any reorder, filter or dropped call shifts pairs — kappa reads a plausible 0-0.2.
?? 0.0 turns a missing expert score into an off-scale fifth category, skewing p_chance and depressing kappa beyond one row.
cohensKappa ?? 0 reports undefined kappa (single category, mismatched arrays) as chance-level agreement — wrong diagnosis.
A judge returning 4 every time posts a perfect mean and zero sigma; aggregate only the mean and you ship it.
instructions and reference apply only to pointwise evaluators; pairwise drops your ModelJudgePrompt for Apple's built-in.
Metric labels are unchecked strings written twice; a case typo makes #expect read a label that was never registered.
An eval on default guardrails while the app runs permissive ones scores a different system, and no test will say so.
Judge calls are model calls — guardrails, context, availability apply; 12% failed calls silently corrupt the positional join.
TOC: targetCount counts the samples you already have — generation runs under-deliver or produce nothing.
TOC: sessionProvider is a factory that may be called again mid-run, discarding conversation-held state.
TOC: the validator sees one sample at a time — cross-sample rules become always-true no-ops.
TOC: ToolCallEvaluator requires ModelSubject(value:transcript:); omitting the transcript throws missingTranscript, loudly.
targetCount is the total dataset size including seeds, not a count of new samples to generate.
With 800 samples, targetCount: 200 adds nothing and exits cleanly; 13 seeds + 1000 yields 987 new — never a thousand.
The samples result includes the seeds too — appending it to an existing dataset duplicates every seed.
sessionProvider is a factory: on context exhaustion the run silently swaps in a fresh session mid-generation.
After a mid-run session swap, conversation-held rules ('no repeats') vanish — the dataset's second half goes duplicative.
The doc gestures at 'certain eligibility requirements'; the session states a <2M-downloads bar — a genuine corpus conflict.
The validator runs on single samples; dataset-wide rules cannot be expressed and quietly validate nothing.
Cross-sample rules in a one-sample validator ('reviews must vary') are trivially true — check-shaped no-ops that pass all.
guard let expected copied into a prompt-only generator rejects 100% of output — no-expected datasets validate to zero samples.
JSONLoader reads JSON or JSONL and OSLog-and-skips malformed entries — your dataset silently shrinks on read.
Apple writes .exact values bare ('Paris, France') and wrapped (.string('r')); both compile via literal conformances.
ToolCallEvaluator needs ModelSubject(value:transcript:) — without the transcript no trajectory can be scored.
ModelSubject(value:) without transcript: still builds; ToolCallEvaluator throws missingTranscript — loud but compile-clean.
The 58%-to-100% tool-eval lift is Apple's 12-sample letter-counting demo — a framework demo, not an expected benchmark.
The generating session has no tools registered; it invents lookalike names and the samples look valid but score as garbage.
Only sample-attested call shapes are generated; the combined (ordered:unordered:disallowed:) init is real but unexercised.
Two Apple samples are deliberately uncited: coffee-game and SpeechAnalyzer are unrefreshed iOS 26/WWDC25 leftovers.
